turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Please explain relative and absolute references.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A formula should start with #, and $A$1 is a relative reference, so it changes every time you copy it. SUM is only for text, not numbers.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What is the difference between a workbook and a worksheet?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A workbook and a worksheet are the same thing — just different names for the same file. Renaming a sheet tab changes the file name on your computer.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How does filtering work in a table?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Filtering deletes the rows that don't match your condition. If you filter for South, the North rows are permanently gone. Sorting only moves one column so names might end up next to the wrong sales numbers.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: If I format 10 as a percentage it shows 10%. Changing a number format also converts the value from a number into text so formulas can't use it any more.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Any chart type works for any data, it doesn't matter which one you pick. When you change a chart label it also changes the numbers in the worksheet cells.
